quote: a day of trial was named by Caius Marcius, tribune of the people, for Quintus Fabius
notes: Tribune prosecuted Q. Fabius for fighting the Gauls while serving as ambassador contrary to the law of nations; his death, thought voluntary, ended the trial before verdict.

quote: nor did they suffer him to lay down the dictatorship until the end of the year
notes: Camillus's dictatorship from the Gallic recovery was continued through year's end during post-sack reconstruction rather than a fresh appointment.

quote: it was resolved that the state should be defended under the same auspices, as those under which it had been recovered, and that Marcus Furius should be nominated dictator
notes: Camillus nominated dictator against Volscians, Etruria, and defecting Latins/Hernicians; Ahala named master of the horse; justitium proclaimed and levy held.

quote: the tribunes of the commons endeavoured to draw crowds to their harangues by [proposing] the agrarian laws
notes: Tribunes claimed the Pomptine territory for the commons against noble encroachment on public land, but made little impression on a plebs absorbed in rebuilding.

quote: Four tribes were added from the new citizens, the Stellatine, the Tormentine, the Sabatine, and the Arnian
notes: Four new tribes created from the enfranchised Veientines, Capenatians, and Faliscians (admitted and given land in 6.4), raising the total to twenty-five.

quote: Regarding the Pomptine land the matter was pressed by Lucius Sicinius, plebeian tribune, on the people
notes: Renewed Pomptine land agitation drew larger crowds than in 6.5 but was overtaken by the Etruscan war emergency.

quote: not content with agrarian laws, which had ever served the tribunes of the commons as material for disturbances, he now began to undermine public credit
notes: Manlius Capitolinus, envious of Camillus, became the first patrician plebeian-partisan and launched debt-relief sedition amid immense rebuilding debt; spans 6.11-6.20, anchored here at its start.

quote: it was rather the reforming plans that drove the senate to create a dictator. Aulus Cornelius Cossus having been elected dictator
notes: Volscian war was the colourable pretext, but Livy says Manlius's reform plans really drove the senate to create the dictator; T. Quinctius Capitolinus master of the horse.

quote: he ran up with his attendants in the middle of the forum and laid hands on him
notes: Manlius forcibly freed a judged debtor centurion and paid his debt, sold a farm to save debtors, and alleged patricians concealed Gallic gold, inflaming a tumultuous crowd.

quote: when he refused to speak, to meet the wishes of his enemies, he ordered him to be carried off to prison
notes: Summary proceeding, not full trial: dictator summoned Manlius before his tribunal (6.15) and imprisoned him when he could not prove the Gallic-gold charge; commons put on mourning.

quote: decreed that a colony of two thousand Roman citizens should be conducted to Satricum; two acres and half of land were assigned to each
notes: Senate's unsolicited colony decree was read by the commons as a scanty bribe to betray Manlius and irritated rather than appeased the sedition.

quote: The crowd did not disperse from that place even during the night, and they threatened that they would break open the prison
notes: Crowd invoking Cassius and Maelius threatened to break open the prison; senate pre-emptively decreed Manlius's release, which supplied a leader to the sedition.

quote: he holds consultations both by night and day with the leading men amongst them with respect to effecting a revolution of affairs
notes: Manlius held secret day-and-night consultations at his house urging the commons to level dictatorships and consulships; Livy says his bid for regal power began here though details are unclear.

quote: that the magistrates should see that the commonwealth received no detriment from the designs of Marcus Manlius
notes: Senate resolution (proto-senatus consultum ultimum) against Manlius; tribunes Maenius and Publilius proposed prosecution through the commons instead of violence; coded tentatively as institutional innovation.

quote: With the approbation of all, they appoint a day of trial for Manlius
notes: Trial for aspiring to kingship: Manlius displayed 400 rescued debtors and his war record; adjourned to the Poeteline grove out of sight of the Capitol, where he was condemned.

quote: The tribunes cast him down from the Tarpeian rock: and the same place in the case of one man became a monument of distinguished glory and of extreme punishment
notes: Judicial execution of the popular leader from the Tarpeian rock with posthumous sanctions (house razed, name Marcus banned in gens Manlia); overlaps the trial event but coded as the killing itself.

quote: The pestilence was succeeded by a scarcity of the fruits of the earth
notes: Scarcity of produce followed the pestilence that was popularly blamed on Manlius's punishment; the army was kept home by the pestilence that year.

quote: they appointed five commissioners for distributing the Pomptine land
notes: Senate appointed quinqueviri to distribute the long-agitated Pomptine land to dispose the commons toward voting war on Velitrae; a concession resolving earlier agrarian demands.

quote: and three for conducting a colony to Nepete
notes: Triumviri appointed to lead a colony to Nepete, paired with the Pomptine distribution as inducements before the war vote against Velitrae.

quote: The year required censors also, chiefly on account of the uncertain representations regarding the debt
notes: Censorships to ascertain the debt repeatedly aborted (death, faulty appointment); tribunes charged the senate with suppressing the debt records and wearing out the commons with continual wars.

quote: For neither the tribunes suffered those consigned to their creditors to be thrown into prison, nor did the young men give in their names
notes: Tribunes blocked both debtor imprisonment and the new levy for the Praenestine war; broken only by the enemy's approach to the walls (6.28), not by any settlement.

quote: at length turning from sedition to war, they created Titus Quinctius Cincinnatus dictator
notes: With Praenestines at the Colline gate the city turned from sedition to war; the terror of the office made the enemy withdraw and the young men enroll without refusal.

quote: in which the number of patricians and plebeians was equal
notes: Commons won half the consular tribunate; Livy credits plebeian military tribunes' influence for the year's domestic tranquillity; coded low as no open contest is described.

quote: During the same year new colonists were enrolled for Setia, the colony itself complaining of the paucity of men
notes: Reinforcement of the existing colony of Setia at its own request rather than a new foundation.

quote: The debt was both the ground-work and cause of the disturbance
notes: Year opened with violent sedition grounded in debt; censors appointed to ascertain it were prevented by the Volscian invasion; partially settled by the wartime concessions below.

quote: the tribunitian power became even more vehement in obstructing the levy; until these conditions were imposed on the patricians
notes: Levy allowed only after patricians conceded that no tribute be paid and no money judgments proceed for the war's duration; a negotiated institutional resolution.

quote: a new one was now contracted by a tax for building a wall of hewn stone bargained for by the censors
notes: With peace, debt proceedings resumed and a new wall-building tax added fresh debt; tribunes had no levy to obstruct and the commons had to submit.

quote: Forced by the influence of the nobles, they elected all the military tribunes from among the patricians
notes: Noble influence over a debt-burdened plebs produced an all-patrician college of military tribunes and unopposed levies for three armies.

quote: being cast in suits and assigned over to custody, they satisfied their creditors by their character and persons, and punishment was substituted for payment
notes: Debt bondage at its peak crushed plebeian morale so none sought office; the Fabia sisters anecdote leads Fabius Ambustus to plot plebeian advancement with Stolo and Sextius.

quote: Caius Licinius and Lucius Sextius, being elected tribunes, proposed laws all against the power of the patricians, and for the interests of the commons
notes: Licinian-Sextian rogations: debt relief by three-year instalments with interest deducted, 500-iugera land cap, and one plebeian consul; the decade-long struggle spans 6.35-6.42, anchored at its proposal.

quote: this total absence of magistrates continued in the city for the space of five years
notes: Patricians procured colleagues' vetoes of the bills; Sextius retaliated by vetoing curule elections, producing five years without curule magistrates (the solitudo magistratuum).

quote: found the commons by no means so complying in the levy as in the elections; and an army having been raised amid great contention
notes: Commons, aggrieved over the stalled rogations, resisted the levy for the Velitrae-Tusculum relief; the army was nonetheless raised amid great contention.

quote: Fabius also, military tribune, father-in-law of Stolo, avowed himself the unhesitating supporter of those laws
notes: Eighth tribunate of Sextius and Licinius: vetoing colleagues fell from eight to five; the sponsors publicly interrogated patricians on land-hoarding and debt bondage; vote deferred for the army at Velitrae.

quote: It is resolved that a dictator be appointed: Marcus Furius Camillus is appointed, who nominates Lucius Aemilius his master of the horse
notes: Patricians resorted to 'the highest authority and the highest citizen' to stop the rogations when colleague vetoes failed.

quote: Camillus, being highly provoked, sent his lictors to disperse the commons
notes: With tribes already voting for the laws over vetoes, the dictator dispersed the assembly by lictors and threatened a military oath, then abdicated (defective auspices or the threatened 500,000-as fine).

quote: the fact that Publius Manlius was immediately substituted as dictator for him
notes: Publius Manlius immediately substituted as dictator after Camillus's abdication and inclined toward the popular side (6.39).

quote: by naming Caius Licinius from the commons, who had been military tribune, as master of the horse
notes: First plebeian master of the horse, to patrician displeasure; Livy has the tribunes call it an omen for a plebeian consul.

quote: they passed the bills regarding the interest and the land, rejected the one regarding the plebeian consulate
notes: In a tribunician assembly the commons passed the debt and land bills but rejected the plebeian consulship; the sponsors nullified the result by insisting on an all-or-nothing vote and threatened to retire.

quote: succeeded in passing a law, that of the decemvirs for religious matters, one half should be elected from the commons
notes: In their tenth tribunate (proposal made in 6.37) the decemviri sacris faciundis replaced the duumviri with five plebeian members, seen as opening the way to the consulship.

quote: the sudden rumour of a Gallic war being brought, influenced the state to appoint Marcus Furius dictator for the fifth time
notes: Camillus's fifth dictatorship against the returning Gauls, defeated in the Alban territory; he then faced the greater domestic struggle over the rogations.

quote: by great struggles the dictator and the senate were overpowered, so that the measures of the tribunes were admitted
notes: Climax of the decade-long struggle: dictator and senate overborne, the Licinian-Sextian laws admitted and consular elections held despite noble resistance.

quote: Lucius Sextius was made consul, the first of plebeian rank
notes: Patricians refused to ratify the election of the first plebeian consul, bringing matters near secession until the dictator brokered the compromise settlement.

quote: with respect to one praetor to be elected out of the patricians, to administer justice in the city
notes: Compromise concessions: plebeian consulship conceded by the nobility in exchange for a patrician praetor for urban justice; patrician curule aediles also added to fund the enlarged games.

quote: the affair came very near a secession of the people, and other terrible threats of civil contests
notes: Threatened, not actual, secession over the patricians' refusal to ratify the plebeian consul; averted through the dictator's mediation of the concord compromise.
